findings.description: "Kept origin/$BRANCH: it moved past the merged tip" is printed on every push failure, including auth, network and branch-protection errors, when the lease only trips if the branch moved after the fetch. Meanwhile the common case where origin really did move past the tip (`REMOTE_TIP != TIP`) skips the push and prints nothing. Use a cause-neutral message on push failure (e.g. "Kept origin/$BRANCH: delete refused (see git's error above)") and add an `else` that reports the moved-past case.

The fetch now runs before the loop and is fatal, so offline or without an `origin` remote the script exits on git's error before removing any worktree. Before this commit those cases still removed clean worktrees and kept their branches. Only the branch deletions need a fresh origin. Keeping the failure closed while still removing worktrees would restore that: on fetch failure, set a flag that skips branch deletion and says why, e.g. `FETCHED=1; git fetch --prune --quiet origin || { FETCHED=0; echo "Fetch failed: keeping all branches" >&2; }`, then `[ "$FETCHED" = 1 ] || continue` after "Removed".

The Worktree removal row hardcodes `feature/` though the script deletes `<prefix>/` branches from WORKTREE_BRANCH_PREFIX, and omits the detached-HEAD case the script header names as a reason a worktree is kept.
